CIVIC EDUCATION
RELIGION AND NATIONAL VALUES
FIRST TERM
WEEK 4
PRIMARY 6
THEME: CIVIC EDUCATION
PREVIOUS LESSON - VALUING NIGERIAN GOODS Primary 6 (Basic 6) - Civic Education
TOPIC: VALUES THAT PROMOTE PEACE - TOLERANCE
LEARNING AREA
1. Introductory Activities
2. Meaning and Types of Values
3. Acceptance Behaviours in our Society
4. Meaning and Characteristics of Tolerance
5. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most of the pupils should have attained the following objectives -
1. explain the meaning of value;
2. state the difference between tolerance and intolerance;
3. mention the characteristics of tolerance;
4. identify values that promote peace.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can differentiate between good behaviour and bad behaviors.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of posters/pictures.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.

Scheme of Work
9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
Course Book
All Relevant Material
Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
Values are the acceptable standard behaviour of people in our society.
There are behaviours that are not acceptable.
Values influence people’s behaviors and attitudes positively or negatively.
Values serve as important guidelines in all situations such as home, community, establishment such as workplace, school, religion etc.
Values are lasting beliefs, ideas, opinions shared by an individual, group or member of a community (culture) about something useful.
TYPES OF VALUES
1. Good values
2. Bad values
GOOD VALUES
Good values are the behaviours that are acceptable in our society.
For example - tolerance, honesty, respect, etc.
BAD VALUES
Bad behaviours the behaviours that are not acceptable in our society.
For example - lying, stealing, killing, etc.
EXAMPLES OF STANDARD VALUES
1. Honesty
2.Tolerance
3. Respect
4. Forgiveness
5. Self-control
6. Humanness
7. Humidity
8. Moderation
8. Justice
9. Peace
10. Fairness
11. Involvement
12. Generosity, etc.
These are examples of values that many people endorse. Good value promote peace.
LESSON 2 - TOLERANCE
Tolerance is one of the acceptable behaviours and values that promote peace in our society.
Tolerance is the willingness to tolerate or accept people’s behavior, beliefs, opinions or practices that a different from your own.
Intolerance is when people cannot accept views, beliefs, or behavior that different from their own.
Tolerance does not mean that you have to do what they do or you have follow their beliefs or practices.
CHARACTERISTICS OF TOLERANCE
1. Respect for each other
2. Behaviour and ways of doing things
3. Forgiveness
4. Accommodation
5. Slow to anger
6. Carefulness
7. Think and rethink before you do anything.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. Revises the previous lesson based on the pupil’s related knowledge or experience.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in the lesson revision.
2. Tells story of good and bad behaviours.
3. Lets pupils state the moral lesson of the story.
Pupil’s Activities - Listen to the teacher’s story and state the moral lessons in the story.
4. Uses the story to introduce the lesson.
5. Displays chart to support your lesson introduction.
Pupil’s Activities - Pay attention to the lesson introduction.
6. Leads discussion on the meaning and types of values.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in the discussion.
7. Lets the pupils items examples of goods and bad behaviours.
Pupil’s Activities - Differentiate between good and bad behaviours with appropriate examples.
8. Explains the meaning of tolerance as one of the examples of good values and its characteristics.
Pupil’s Activities - Define and state the characteristics of tolerance.
9. Summarizes the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as instructed.
CONCLUSION
- To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
- Next Lesson - Values that Promote Peace - Cooperation Primary 6 (Basic 6) - Civic Education

Ask pupils to:
1. explain the meaning of values.
2. differentiate between good and bad behaviours.
3. State 6 examples of acceptable behaviour in your society.
4. List 5 examples of acceptable behaviour in our school.
6. explain the meaning of tolerance.
7. mention 5 characteristics of tolerance.
WORKBOOK

A. Goods
B. Bads
C. Values
2. Good values are the behaviours that are ________ in our society.
A. unacceptable
B. acceptance
C. bad values
3. Bad values are the behaviours that are ________ in our society.
A. unacceptable
B. acceptance
C. bad values
4. ________ is the willingness to tolerate or accept people’s behavior, beliefs, opinions or practices that a different from your own.
A. Intolerance
B. Tolerance
C. Acceptable
5. ________ is when people cannot accept views, beliefs, or behavior that different from their own.
A. Intolerance
B. Tolerance
C. Acceptable
6. Tolerance does not mean that you have to do what they do or you have follow their beliefs or practices.
A. True
B. False
7. There are behaviours that are not acceptable.
A. False
B. True
8. Values influence people’s behaviors and attitudes positively or negatively.
A. True
B. False
9. Values serve cannot as important guidelines in all situations such as home, community, establishment (work, school, religion etc.).
A. True
B. False

A. True
B. False

INTRODUCTION
Unity is the act of working as a single force composed of different people, organization, bodies, states, or nations.
One Nigeria means being as one people and making sure everyone shares the true identity of one nation.
MEANING OF NATIONAL UNITY
National unity is ability to accept other people from different ethnics or groups as one, irrespective of religion, status, culture and geographical location.
THINGS THAT CONSTITUTE NATIONAL UNITY
1. Emphasizing things that unites us,
2. Respecting the national objectives, coat of arms,
3. Strengthening national bonds.
LESSON 2 - IMPORTANCE OF NATIONAL UNITY
1. It brings about the national development.
2. It helps the government of the nation to understand the people’s need and choices.
3. It strengthens a nation.
4. It brings about safety in a nation.
5. National unity and integration encourages People to share ideas, values and emotional bonds.

NATIONAL HONOURS AWARD: DEFINITION AND MEANING OF NATIONAL HONOURS AWARDS AND TYPES OF NATIONAL HONOURS AWARDS
CIVIC EDUCATION
PRIMARY 6 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 1
THEME - NATIONAL VALUES EDUCATION
PREVIOUS LESSON - First Term, Second Term and Third Term Civic Education Plan Lesson Notes and Scheme of Work for Primary 5 (Basic 5)
TOPIC - NATIONAL HONOURS AWARD
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Meaning of National Honours Awards and National Honours
3. Types of National Honours Awards in Nigeria
4. Types and Importance of National Honours Awards
5. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
6. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Define national honours awards.
2. Explain the meaning of a national honour.
3. Mention at least five types of national honours awards in Nigeria.
4. Identify some people who may qualify for national honours based on their contributions to the country.
5. State the importance of national honours awards to Nigeria.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about good citizenship, national values, patriotism, and the responsibilities of citizens.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by introducing national honours awards as a way the Nigerian government recognises and appreciates people who have made outstanding contributions to the country.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Pictures of Nigerian national honours medals and insignia
2. Chart showing the different types of national honours
3. Pictures of notable national award recipients
4. Flashcards
5. Civic Education textbook
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
People who serve their country through outstanding achievements and contributions deserve recognition and appreciation. Governments therefore give special awards to citizens who have distinguished themselves in areas such as public service, education, medicine, science, business, sports, arts, security, and community development.
In Nigeria, these special recognitions are known as National Honours Awards. They encourage citizens to serve the country, work hard, and contribute to national development.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about the meaning of national honours awards, their types, and their importance to Nigeria.
MEANING OF NATIONAL HONOURS AWARDS
National Honours Awards are special awards given by the government to Nigerian citizens who have made outstanding contributions to the development, unity, security, or progress of Nigeria.
They are a way of recognising and appreciating people who have served the country or made significant contributions to society.
MEANING OF NATIONAL HONOURS
A national honour is a special recognition given by the Nigerian government to a person for distinguished service or achievement.
National honours may be given to people who have made important contributions in areas such as:
- Public service
- Education
- Medicine
- Business
- Science and technology
- Arts and culture
- Sports
- Security
- Community development
TYPES OF NATIONAL HONOURS AWARDS IN NIGERIA
The Nigerian national honours are arranged into different classes.
1. Grand Commander of the Order of the Federal Republic (GCFR) - The GCFR is the highest national honour in Nigeria. It is traditionally associated with the President of Nigeria.
2. Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger (GCON) - The GCON is the second-highest national honour. It is awarded to Nigerians who have rendered outstanding service to the nation.
3. Commander of the Order of the Federal Republic (CFR) - The CFR is awarded to people who have made distinguished contributions to Nigeria.
4. Commander of the Order of the Niger (CON) - The CON is awarded to Nigerians who have made significant contributions to the development and progress of the country.
5. Officer of the Order of the Federal Republic (OFR) - The OFR recognises distinguished service or contributions to the nation.
6. Officer of the Order of the Niger (OON) - The OON is awarded to people who have rendered valuable service to Nigeria.
7. Member of the Order of the Federal Republic (MFR) - The MFR recognises notable contributions to the nation.
8. Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) - The MON is given to people who have made valuable contributions to the country or society.
IMPORTANCE OF NATIONAL HONOURS AWARDS
National honours awards are important because they:
1. Recognise outstanding service to Nigeria.
2. Encourage citizens to serve their country.
3. Appreciate people who contribute to national development.
4. Promote patriotism and national unity.
5. Encourage hard work and excellence.
6. Inspire younger people to make positive contributions to society.
ON A FINAL NOTE
- National Honours Awards are important forms of recognition given by the Nigerian government to people who have made outstanding contributions to the country.
- They encourage patriotism, service, hard work, excellence, and national development.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. National Honours Awards are special awards given by the Nigerian government to people who have made ______.
A. outstanding contributions to the country
B. harmful contributions
C. no contribution
D. private complaints
2. The highest national honour in Nigeria is ______.
A. MON
B. OON
C. GCFR
D. MFR
3. Which of the following is a type of National Honours Award?
A. NAFDAC
B. NYSC
C. WAEC
D. GCON l
4. National honours help to encourage citizens to ______.
A. break laws
B. serve their country
C. avoid responsibility
D. discourage others
4. A person may receive a national honour for outstanding contributions in ______.
A. education
B. crime
C. dishonesty
D. violence
B. Fill in the Gaps
6. A special recognition given by the government for distinguished service is called a national ______.
7. ______ is the highest national honour in Nigeria.
8. GCON means Grand Commander of the Order of the ______.
9. MON means Member of the Order of the ______.
10. National honours can encourage ______ and hard work among citizens.
C. True or False
11. National honours are given to recognise outstanding contributions to Nigeria. ______
12. GCFR is one of Nigeria’s national honours. ______
13. National honours encourage citizens to contribute positively and negatively to national development. ______
14. National honours are given only to people in the entertainment industry. ______
15. National honours can promote patriotism and national unity. ______
D. Matching
11. GCFR - A. Commander of the Order of the Niger
12. GCON - B. Member of the Order of the Niger
13. CON - C. Grand Commander of the Order of the Federal Republic
14. OON - D. Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger
15. MON - E. Officer of the Order of the Niger
ANSWER KEY
1. A - Outstanding contributions to the country
2. C - GCFR
3. D - GCON
4. B - Serve their country
5. A - Education
6. Honour
7. GCFR
8. Niger
9. Niger
10. Patriotism
11. True
12. True
13. False
14. False
15. True
11. C - Grand Commander of the Order of the Federal Republic
12. D - Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger
13. A - Commander of the Order of the Niger
14. E - Officer of the Order of the Niger
15. B - Member of the Order of the Niger
SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that National Honours Awards are special recognitions given by the Nigerian government to people who have made outstanding contributions to the development, unity, security, or progress of Nigeria.
They learned that national honours may be awarded to people who have distinguished themselves in areas such as education, public service, medicine, business, science and technology, sports, arts, security, and community development.
Some types of National Honours Awards in Nigeria include:
- GCFR - Grand Commander of the Order of the Federal Republic.
- GCON - Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger.
- CFR - Commander of the Order of the Federal Republic.
- CON - Commander of the Order of the Niger.
- OFR - Officer of the Order of the Federal Republic.
- OON - Officer of the Order of the Niger.
- MFR - Member of the Order of the Federal Republic.
- MON - Member of the Order of the Niger.
Pupils also learned that national honours help to recognise outstanding service, encourage patriotism, promote hard work, and inspire citizens to contribute to national development.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher asks pupils:
- Have you ever received an award for doing something well?
- Why do people receive awards?
- Who gives national awards in Nigeria?
- What type of person deserves to be honoured by the nation?
The teacher explains that people who make outstanding contributions to their country can be recognised and appreciated through special awards.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions and mention examples of awards they know.
Step 2: Meaning of National Honours Awards
The teacher explains that National Honours Awards are special awards given by the Nigerian government to people who have made outstanding contributions to the development, unity, security, or progress of Nigeria.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the meaning of National Honours Awards in their own words.
Step 3: Meaning of National Honour
The teacher explains that a national honour is a special recognition given to a person for distinguished service or achievement that benefits the nation.
The teacher explains that people from different fields can receive national honours.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention areas in which people can make outstanding contributions to Nigeria.
Step 4: Types of National Honours Awards
The teacher introduces the major types of national honours in Nigeria:
- GCFR - Grand Commander of the Order of the Federal Republic.
- GCON - Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger.
- CFR - Commander of the Order of the Federal Republic.
- CON - Commander of the Order of the Niger.
- OFR - Officer of the Order of the Federal Republic.
- OON - Officer of the Order of the Niger.
- MFR - Member of the Order of the Federal Republic.
- MON - Member of the Order of the Niger.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils read and repeat the names and meanings of the different honours.
Step 5: Highest National Honour
The teacher explains that GCFR (Grand Commander of the Order of the Federal Republic) is the highest national honour in Nigeria.
The teacher also explains that GCON (Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger) is another very high national honour.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify the highest national honour and state its full meaning.
Step 6: Who Can Receive National Honours?
The teacher explains that national honours may be given to people who have made outstanding contributions in areas such as:
- Public service
- Education
- Medicine
- Science and technology
- Business
- Sports
- Arts and culture
- Security
- Community development
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention people or professions that may receive national honours.
Step 7: Importance of National Honours Awards
The teacher explains that national honours:
- Recognise outstanding service to Nigeria.
- Encourage citizens to serve their country.
- Appreciate people who contribute to national development.
- Promote patriotism and national unity.
- Encourage hard work and excellence.
- Inspire young people to make positive contributions.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention the importance of national honours.
Step 8: Group Activity
The teacher divides pupils into four groups.
- Group 1: Explain the meaning of National Honours Awards.
- Group 2: List four types of national honours.
- Group 3: Mention five areas where a person can make an outstanding contribution to Nigeria.
- Group 4: State five importance of National Honours Awards.
Each group presents its answers to the class.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write, and present their answers.
Step 9: Lesson Summary
The teacher reviews the meaning, types, and importance of National Honours Awards and emphasises the value of patriotism, hard work, and service to the nation.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer oral questions and summarise what they have learned.
Step 10: Evaluation
The teacher gives pupils a different set of 20 questions as oral questions, a quiz, take-home work, or a quick test to assess their understanding of National Honours Awards.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions individually or in groups.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Examples of People Rewarded with National Honour: National Heroes and Heroines and the National Honours They Received | Primary 6 (Basic 6) First Term Week 2 Civic Education
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils,
1. What are National Honours Awards?
2. Explain the meaning of a national honour.
3. Mention five types of National Honours Awards in Nigeria.
4. What does GCFR stand for?
5. State four importance of National Honours Awards.
6. Mention three areas in which a person may make an outstanding contribution to qualify for a national honour.

EXAMPLES OF PEOPLE REWARDED WITH NATIONAL HONOUR: NATIONAL HEROES AND HEROINES AND THE NATIONAL HONOURS THEY RECEIVED
SOCIAL STUDIES
PRIMARY 6 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 2
THEME - NATIONAL VALUES EDUCATION
PREVIOUS LESSON - National Honours Award: Definition and Meaning of National Honours Awards and Types of National Honours Awards | Primary 6 (Basic 6) First Term Week 1 Civic Education
TOPIC - EXAMPLES OF PEOPLE REWARDED WITH NATIONAL HONOUR
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Meaning of National Heroes and Heroines
3. Examples of Nigerians Who Received National Honours
4. Importance of Recognising National Heroes and Heroines
5. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
6. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain who national heroes and heroines are.
2. Mention at least five Nigerians who have received national honours.
3. Identify the national honours received by selected Nigerian heroes and heroines.
4. State the contributions of some national heroes and heroines to Nigeria.
5. Explain why national heroes and heroines should be recognised and honoured.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about National Honours Awards, their meaning, types, and importance.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by introducing pupils to examples of Nigerians who have received national honours and the contributions that earned them national recognition.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Pictures of Nigerian national heroes and heroines
2. Charts showing names and national honours received
3. Pictures or charts of national honour medals and insignia
4. Flashcards
5. Civic Education textbook
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Some Nigerians have made outstanding contributions to the development, unity, freedom, and progress of the country. The Nigerian government recognises some of these contributions by giving deserving people National Honours Awards.
People who have made significant contributions to the nation may be remembered as national heroes and heroines. Their achievements can inspire younger Nigerians to serve their country and contribute positively to society.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about examples of Nigerian national heroes and heroines, the contributions they made, and the national honours they received.
MEANING OF NATIONAL HEROES AND HEROINES
National heroes and heroines are people (Males and Famales) who have made outstanding contributions to the development, unity, freedom, peace, or progress of Nigeria. Their contributions may be recognised through national honours.
They may come from different fields, including politics, education, public service, science, business, sports, arts, and community development.
EXAMPLES OF NIGERIANS WHO RECEIVED NATIONAL HONOURS
1. Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe - Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe was one of Nigeria’s important nationalist leaders and became the country’s first President.
He was awarded the Grand Commander of the Order of the Federal Republic (GCFR).
2. Chief Obafemi Awolowo - Chief Obafemi Awolowo was a prominent Nigerian statesman who contributed greatly to education, governance, and national development.
He received the Grand Commander of the Order of the Federal Republic (GCFR).
3. Sir Ahmadu Bello - Sir Ahmadu Bello was a prominent Nigerian statesman and the first Premier of Northern Nigeria.
He was awarded the Grand Commander of the Order of the Federal Republic (GCFR).
4. Chief Anthony Enahoro - Chief Anthony Enahoro was a Nigerian nationalist and politician who played an important role in Nigeria’s struggle for self-government and independence.
He was awarded the Commander of the Order of the Federal Republic (CFR).
5. Professor Wole Soyinka - Professor Wole Soyinka is a Nigerian writer, playwright, poet, and academic. He became the first African to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.
He was awarded the Order of the Federal Republic (OFR).
6. Alhaji Aliko Dangote - Aliko Dangote is a Nigerian businessman and philanthropist who has contributed to Nigeria’s economy through business and philanthropy.
He has received national recognition for his contributions to Nigeria.
7. Chief Gani Fawehinmi - Chief Gani Fawehinmi was a Nigerian lawyer, human rights activist, and philanthropist who advocated for justice and human rights.
He was awarded the Member of the Order of the Federal Republic (MFR).
8. Professor Dora Akunyili - Nigerian pharmacist, academic, and former Director-General of NAFDAC.
She received the Member of the Order of the Federal Republic (MFR) for her contributions to public service and the fight against counterfeit drugs.
9. Professor Grace Alele-Williams - Nigerian mathematician and educationist who became the first Nigerian woman to earn a PhD and the first female Vice-Chancellor of a Nigerian university.
She received the Order of the Niger (OON).
IMPORTANCE OF RECOGNISING NATIONAL HEROES AND HEROINES
Recognising national heroes and heroines is important because it:
1. Appreciates their contributions to Nigeria.
2. Encourages patriotism.
3. Inspires young people to serve the country.
4. Promotes hard work and excellence.
5. Preserves the memory of important national contributions.
6. Encourages citizens to contribute positively to society.
ON A FINAL NOTE

Pupils also learned that recognising national heroes and heroines appreciates their contributions, promotes patriotism, encourages hard work, and inspires young people to serve Nigeria.

Step 5: Sir Ahmadu Bello

Step 6: Chief Anthony Enahoro

Step 8: Chief Gani Fawehinmi

Step 9: Importance of Recognising National Heroes and Heroines

- Promotes hard work and excellence.

Step 11: Lesson Summary
The teacher reviews the meaning of national heroes and heroines, the examples studied, their contributions, and the importance of recognising them.

Step 12: Evaluation

ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about National Honours Awards, their meaning, types, and examples of Nigerians who have received national honours.

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Some Nigerians have made outstanding contributions to the development and progress of the country through their work and service. Such contributions may be recognised through National Honours Awards.
National honours show appreciation for people who have served the country, achieved excellence, promoted peace and unity, or made valuable contributions in areas such as education, medicine, science, business, sports, arts, and public service.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about the reasons for National Honours Awards and the areas of service and contribution that may be recognised with national honours.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF NATIONAL HONOURS AWARDS
National Honours Awards are special awards given by the Nigerian government to recognise and honour citizens and other individuals who have made outstanding contributions to the development, peace, unity, security, or progress of Nigeria.
REASONS FOR NATIONAL HONOURS AWARDS
National honours are given for several reasons:
1. To recognise outstanding contributions - They acknowledge people who have made significant contributions to Nigeria.
2. To appreciate national service - They show appreciation to people who have served the country faithfully.
3. To encourage patriotism - National honours encourage citizens to love and serve their country.
4. To promote hard work and excellence - They motivate people to work hard and achieve excellence in their different fields.
5. To inspire younger generations - Honoured individuals can serve as role models for young Nigerians.
6. To encourage selfless service - The awards recognise people who put the interests of society and the nation above personal interests.
7. To promote national unity - Honouring people who contribute to peace and unity can encourage citizens to work together.
8. To preserve national achievements - National honours help the country remember people who have made important contributions to national development.
LESSON 2 - EXAMPLES OF CONTRIBUTIONS THAT MAY BE RECOGNISED
People may receive national honours for contributions in areas such as:
- Education: Outstanding service or contribution to teaching and learning in Nigeria.
- Politics and public service: Outstanding service to the government and the Nigerian people.
- Science and technology: Important contributions to scientific discoveries and technological development.
- Medicine: Outstanding service in improving healthcare and saving lives.
- Business and industry: Significant contributions to business, industry, employment, and economic growth.
- Arts and culture: Contributions to Nigerian arts, literature, music, drama, and cultural development.
- Sports: Outstanding achievements that bring honour and recognition to Nigeria through sports.
- Human rights and community development: Contributions to protecting people’s rights and improving communities.
- National unity and peace: Contributions to promoting peace, unity, cooperation, and peaceful coexistence in Nigeria.
IMPORTANCE OF NATIONAL HONOURS AWARDS
National honours encourage citizens to contribute positively to society. They also remind people that service, dedication, integrity, excellence, and patriotism are valuable qualities.
ON A FINAL NOTE
- National Honours Awards are given to recognise outstanding service and contributions to Nigeria.
- They appreciate deserving individuals, encourage patriotism and excellence, inspire younger people, promote national unity, and preserve the memory of important national achievements.

SUMMARY

THEME - NATIONAL VALUES EDUCATION

LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Meaning of Valuing Nigerian Goods
3. Reasons Why We should Value Nigeria Goods
4. Examples of Nigerian Goods
5. Importance of Valuing Nigerian Goods
6. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
7. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of valuing Nigerian goods.
2. State at least five reasons why Nigerian goods should be valued.
3. Mention at least five examples of Nigerian-made goods.
4. Explain how valuing Nigerian goods can support the Nigerian economy.
5. State the importance of buying quality Nigerian-made goods.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have previously learned about the concept of valuing Nigerian goods, including how to identify Nigerian-made goods and assess their worth based on quality, durability, usefulness, price, and economic value.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by helping pupils understand why Nigerian goods should be valued and examples of Nigerian-made products.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Samples of Nigerian-made goods
2. Pictures of Nigerian products
3. Product labels and packages
4. Charts showing locally made goods

METHOD OF TEACHING

Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.

CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Nigerians use different goods every day, including food, clothing, shoes, furniture, bags, beverages, and household products. Many of these goods are produced by Nigerian farmers, artisans, businesses, and industries.
Valuing Nigerian goods means appreciating and supporting quality products made in Nigeria. When people buy and use quality Nigerian-made goods, they support local businesses, encourage production, create employment, and contribute to national economic development.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about the reasons why we should value Nigerian goods, the importance of valuing them, and examples of Nigerian-made goods.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF VALUING NIGERIAN GOODS
Valuing Nigerian goods means appreciating, supporting, and choosing quality products made in Nigeria. It involves recognising the usefulness and importance of locally produced goods.
REASONS WHY WE SHOULD VALUE NIGERIAN GOODS
We should value Nigerian goods because they:
1. Create employment: Buying local products supports businesses that employ Nigerians.
2. Support local businesses: It helps Nigerian producers, farmers, artisans, and manufacturers to grow.
3. Promote economic development: Local production and sales contribute to the growth of the Nigerian economy.
4. Encourage local industries: Demand for Nigerian goods encourages more people to establish and expand industries.
5. Promote entrepreneurship: Supporting local products encourages people to start and develop businesses.
6. Develop local skills: Production helps Nigerians gain and improve useful skills.
7. Reduce excessive dependence on imports: Using quality local products can reduce unnecessary reliance on foreign goods.
8. Promote national pride: Valuing Nigerian products encourages citizens to appreciate what their country produces.
LESSON 2 - EXAMPLES OF NIGERIAN GOODS
Examples of Nigerian-made goods include:
1. Food products: Garri, Nigerian rice, palm oil, yam flour, and processed food products.
2. Clothing and textiles: Nigerian-made clothes, Ankara garments, and traditional fabrics.
3. Footwear and leather products: Shoes, sandals, belts, and bags made in Nigeria.
4. Furniture: Tables, chairs, beds, and cupboards made by Nigerian producers.
5. Building materials: Cement, blocks, tiles, and other locally produced materials.
6. Beverages: Locally produced soft drinks, fruit drinks, and other beverages.
7. Household products: Soap, detergents, and other locally manufactured products.
8. Agricultural products: Cocoa, cassava, maize, beans, palm products, and other farm produce.
LESSON 3 - IMPORTANCE OF VALUING NIGERIAN GOODS
Valuing Nigerian goods helps to:
1. Improve the income of local producers.
2. Create more employment opportunities.
3. Strengthen local industries.
4. Encourage quality production.
5. Promote entrepreneurship.
6. Support national economic growth.
7. Reduce unnecessary dependence on imported goods.
8. Build national pride and patriotism.
ON A FINAL NOTE
- Valuing Nigerian goods means supporting quality products made in Nigeria.
- By buying and using good Nigerian-made products, citizens can support local businesses, create employment, encourage production, develop local skills, and contribute to the economic development of Nigeria.

SUMMARY
In this lesson, pupils learned that valuing Nigerian goods means appreciating, supporting, and choosing quality products made in Nigeria.
They learned that Nigerian goods should be valued because they support local businesses, create employment, encourage local industries, promote entrepreneurship, develop local skills, reduce excessive dependence on imports, promote national pride, and contribute to economic development.
Pupils also learned examples of Nigerian-made goods, including food products, clothing, footwear, leather products, furniture, building materials, beverages, household products, and agricultural products.

Step 1: Introduction
The teacher asks pupils:
- What are Nigerian-made goods?
- Can you mention some goods made in Nigeria?
- Why should we buy quality Nigerian-made goods?

Step 2: Meaning of Valuing Nigerian Goods

Step 3: Reasons for Valuing Nigerian Goods

- Promote entrepreneurship.

- Reduce excessive dependence on imported goods.
- Promote national pride.

- Clothing and textiles

- Furniture

INTRODUCTION
People use different goods every day, and many of these goods are produced in Nigeria. Patronising Nigerian goods means buying, using, and supporting quality products made in Nigeria.

LESSON 1 - MEANING OF PATRONISING NIGERIAN GOODS
Patronising Nigerian goods means buying, using, and supporting quality products made or produced in Nigeria.
It involves choosing good Nigerian-made products when they are available and meet the required standards.
BENEFITS OF PATRONISING NIGERIAN GOODS
1. It creates employment: It helps local businesses grow and employ more Nigerians.
2. It supports local businesses: It increases sales and income for Nigerian producers and businesses.
3. It encourages local production: Increased demand motivates producers to manufacture more goods.
4. It promotes entrepreneurship: It encourages people to establish and develop businesses.
5. It develops local skills: More production provides opportunities for Nigerians to learn and improve useful skills.
6. It supports economic growth: Increased local production and business activities contribute to national economic development.
7. It reduces excessive dependence on imports: Buying quality local products can reduce unnecessary reliance on foreign goods.
8. It promotes national pride: Using good Nigerian-made products encourages citizens to appreciate what Nigeria can produce.
9. It encourages better quality: When consumers support good products and demand quality, producers are encouraged to improve their products.
10. It increases government revenue: Successful businesses contribute to government revenue through lawful taxes and other payments.

2. Provide employment opportunities.
3. Improve the income of producers and workers.
4. Encourage investment in local industries.
5. Promote self-reliance.
6. Develop Nigerian skills and technology.
7. Strengthen the Nigerian economy.
8. Promote patriotism and national pride.

INTRODUCTION
People use different products every day, including goods made in Nigeria. Developing a positive attitude towards Nigerian goods means appreciating, using, trusting, and supporting quality products made in Nigeria.
However, some problems can make it difficult for people to develop positive attitudes towards Nigerian goods, such as poor quality, poor packaging, high prices, negative perceptions, and preference for foreign goods.
In this lesson, pupils will learn about the problems of developing positive attitudes towards Made-in-Nigeria goods and ways to demonstrate positive attitudes towards them.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF POSITIVE ATTITUDE TOWARDS NIGERIAN GOODS
A positive attitude towards Made-in-Nigeria goods means appreciating, trusting, using, and supporting quality products made in Nigeria.
PROBLEMS OF DEVELOPING POSITIVE ATTITUDES
1. Poor quality: Some local products may not meet expected standards.
2. Poor packaging: Unattractive packaging may discourage consumers.
3. Preference for foreign goods: Some people believe foreign products are better.
4. High prices: Some Nigerian products may be expensive.
5. Negative perception: Some people have a negative opinion of local products.
6. Poor advertising: Limited promotion can make local products less known.
7. Lack of awareness: Consumers may not know about available Nigerian-made products.
8. Counterfeit products: Fake products can reduce people’s trust in local brands.
LESSON 2 - WAYS TO DEMONSTRATE POSITIVE ATTITUDES
1. Buy quality Nigerian goods: Choose good locally made products when available.
2. Use Nigerian products: Regularly use quality Made-in-Nigeria goods.
3. Recommend local products: Encourage family and friends to buy quality Nigerian goods.
4. Promote local products: Tell others about good Nigerian products.
5. Avoid unfair criticism: Judge products based on their quality rather than their origin.
6. Support local businesses: Buy from Nigerian producers and businesses.
7. Take care of Nigerian products: Use and maintain them properly.
8. Give useful feedback: Encourage producers to improve their products.
LESSON 3 - IMPORTANCE OF POSITIVE ATTITUDES
Developing positive attitudes towards Nigerian goods can:
1. Support local businesses.
2. Create employment.
3. Encourage local production.
4. Promote entrepreneurship.
5. Develop local industries.
6. Reduce excessive dependence on imported goods.
7. Promote national pride.
8. Contribute to economic development.
ON A FINAL NOTE
- Positive attitudes towards Made-in-Nigeria goods involve appreciating, using, supporting, and promoting quality local products.
- Although poor quality, high prices, poor packaging, negative perceptions, and preference for foreign goods may make this difficult, citizens can demonstrate positive attitudes by buying, using, recommending, and supporting quality Nigerian-made goods.
